# US-002 — Remove the DAG wave scheduler and lock-list serialization

**Story:** US-002
**Task:** T-002 (status: done)
**Priority:** P1
**Spec:** SPEC-014 FR4, FR6a, FR9, FR9a

---

## Who this affects

Developers using `/planr-pipeline:ship` with the `--max-parallel` flag or relying on the wave-scheduler's automatic serialization of conflicting tasks. Both behaviors are gone.

## What was done

The DAG wave serialization engine that SPEC-013 introduced in `procedures/ship-step2-dag-dispatch.md` §1–§4 was removed entirely. This included:

- **Write-set normalization (§1)** — the procedure that expanded declared file paths to normalized sets for overlap comparison.
- **Cycle detection (§2)** — the check that aborted a dispatch (dispatching nothing) when task dependencies formed a cycle.
- **Lock-list-driven serialization (§3)** — any two tasks touching `package.json`, lockfiles, `**/index.ts`, migrations, or other lock-list paths were forced into separate waves. This logic is gone. The lock-list content itself survives, but only as text advisory hints in the dispatch prompt.
- **Greedy wave selection (§4)** — the algorithm that selected a maximal set of write-disjoint tasks for each wave. Gone.

Additional removals:

- **`--max-parallel` flag removed** from `procedures/ship-arguments-and-cost-gate.md`. The `$SHIP_MAX_PARALLEL` binding, the cost-gate parallelism multiplier (which scaled estimate ranges by the concurrency factor), and all wave/lock-list-enforcement wording in that file are gone. The cost gate still prints a token and dollar estimate — it just has no concurrency knob. Phase A outputs no longer include a parallelism binding.
- **R11 (Wave Write-Safety) removed** from `docs/rules.md`. The rules file stops at R10. No replacement rule was added; the native dispatch behavior is described in `commands/ship.md` and the supporting procedure.

## What survived

The lock-list file paths (`package.json`, lockfiles, `**/index.ts`, `prisma/schema.prisma`, `**/migrations/**`) are kept as a non-enforcing advisory list in `procedures/ship-step2-dag-dispatch.md` Section 2, explicitly labelled "ADVISORY ONLY — surfaced in the dispatch prompt; enforces nothing." When the dispatch loop sees two eligible tasks with declared write-sets that overlap a lock-list path, it adds a plain-text note to each affected task's prompt. This note changes no control flow; the host may act on it or ignore it.

## Acceptance criteria (as verified by QA)

- `docs/rules.md` contains no R11 section or "Wave Write-Safety" heading.
- `procedures/ship-arguments-and-cost-gate.md` contains no `--max-parallel`, no `$SHIP_MAX_PARALLEL`, and no parallelism cost multiplier.
- Lock-list content is retained in `procedures/ship-step2-dag-dispatch.md` Section 2 as advisory-only.
- The cost gate still prints a structured estimate block.
- Given two tasks both declaring `package.json` as a modified file, the dispatch logic emits them in the same turn with no serialization.

All criteria verified PASS by QA Agent (see `qa-report.md` T-002 section).
